# QUESTIONS — Meridian / Zhao (§8 non-compete)

**Status: 2026-10-25.** The client answered Part A/B in part and states it has **no additional information** on the rest. Per that instruction, answered questions are not repeated; what remains is (I) the answers received and where they changed the analysis, (II) **flagged unknowns** (recorded, not re-asked), and (III) decisions only the client can make. The bottom line is unchanged: **do not file in Travis County; do not assert §8.**

## I. Answers received 2026-10-25 (already absorbed into the memo)

| Old # | Client's answer | Where it landed |
|---|---|---|
| Q4, Q20 | "**No evidence he took anything.** He said he wouldn't." | Memo §3 (now a fact, not an assumption); §6 item 3 — a trade-secrets claim has no factual predicate and must not be pleaded or threatened. |
| Q5 | "**It's the competing itself we object to.**" | Memo §5 — Meridian's own framing concedes the only grievance is competition, which §16600 (as amended) makes non-cognizable in California. This is the client's most damaging admission and it is now in Zhao's best-case list. |
| Q8 | "**Legal ops never sent the notices. The ticket was closed as 'won't do.'**" | Memo §3, §4.5, §7.4 — the (b) violation is complete and **documented as a knowing decision** for every California engineer current on 2024-02-14. Worse than "deprioritized." |
| Q9 | "**No. It's our standard form; engineers sign the same day. Nobody negotiates.**" | Memo §3, §5 — the §925(e) "individually negotiated with counsel" exception is unavailable for **every** engineer on the form; there is no defensible variant anywhere in the population. |
| Q7 (partial) | The present-tense "engineers sign the same day" implies the form is **still in use**. | Treated as an open risk in §6 item 5 (stop today) and flagged below. |

The client also asked that the LO-233 "won't do" fact be kept out of writing. That instruction **could not be accommodated** and is addressed candidly in memo §4.5 ("Your 10/25 instruction..."): the fact already exists in the ticket and in the client's own email; deletion or cleanup is off the table (litigation hold); the fix is remediation (notices + form change) through privileged channels, not documentation management.

## II. Flagged unknowns (client has no additional information — recorded, not re-asked)

1. **Demand letter status (was most urgent).** Whether any §8/§9 demand, cease, or stop-work communication ever went to Zhao or Kestrel remains unconfirmed. **If one went out, §7.2's §16600.5(b) exposure already accrued** — memo §8 item 2. Verify from Meridian's own outgoing-correspondence files, not recollection; this does not require new information from anyone, only a records pull.
2. **Kestrel start.** Whether Zhao in fact started at Kestrel on/about 2026-10-13 (HR-timeline assumption stands) — memo §8 item 1.
3. **Pre-2024 Meridian employment.** If Zhao was employed before 2024-02-14 under an earlier agreement, the §16600.1(b) timing wrinkle — the *only* defense in this file — collapses for him too — memo §8 item 4.
4. **Headcount and dates (drives the only real number).** Number of California-resident engineers on the §8 form, broken out by hire date vs. **2024-02-14** (§16600.1(b) deadline) and **2024-01-01** (§16600.5), plus departures. The §7.4 table is linear in N and stays illustrative. Pull from HR systems, not memory.
5. **Form's usage window.** Since when the current form has been used, and whether California-resident hires are still being put on it (§7 partial answer above). Every post-2024-01-01 California hire is a fresh §16600.5(c) violation.
6. **Full agreement.** Whether a prevailing-party fee clause, arbitration clause, merger clause, or PIIA exists anywhere outside the excerpt; what §10 actually delivers in defined confidential information (the Sheshunoff "ancillary" element in the Texas-law branch) — memo §8 item 3.
7. **Alvarez / *Westbrook* / *Calderon*.** Status of the 2024 memo's recommended Travis County suit (filed? on this form? California-based employee?), and the current status of *Westbrook* en banc and *Calderon* — **neither is in this library**, and *Westbrook* is the one authority in the firm's file that could help, currently unverifiable. Needs someone with subscription access.

## III. Decisions still awaiting the client (no information needed — only authorization)

1. **Stop the form for California-resident hires — today** (§6 item 5). Weeks of continued use are accruals, not delay.
2. **Authorize the §16600.1(b)-style notices** to current and qualifying former California employees, and reopen LO-233 as a compliance record (§6 item 6; §4.5 remediation judgment call). The "won't do" closure stands until someone reverses it.
3. **Confirm the litigation hold**, including LO-233 exactly as closed (§6 item 7).
4. **Objective check.** The 10/25 answer ("the competing itself") reads as a pure non-compete/deterrence interest. If that is the real goal, say so — the answer is still "don't file," but the follow-on work is §10 discipline, lawful protections, and future Texas-hire drafting, a different memo.
